governing_rule: Reuse shared software and evidence contracts; localize experience, architecture, operations, ecology, culture, economics and regulations through site-specific profiles.
non_claims: A profile label does not establish site suitability.
All climate, demand, cost and ecological values remain unknown unless bound to a cited dataset, local survey or qualified measurement.
A synthetic model is not a coastal-engineering, aquatic-safety, maritime-emissions, avalanche-safety, accessibility or ecological certification.
Cultural experiences require local rights-holders and communities to direct, consent to and benefit from their representation.

reusable_rules.name: No label-based siting
reusable_rules.rule: Country, climate-zone or biome labels can suggest questions but cannot infer project suitability, carrying capacity, cultural permission, legal status or numeric model parameters.

reusable_rules.name: Separate observation, model and authority
reusable_rules.rule: A measured condition, a forecast, an adopted policy, an operating command, a permit and a verified outcome are separate typed records.

reusable_rules.name: Hard limits stay hard
reusable_rules.rule: Law, public safety, water quality, rights, accessibility obligations, protected habitat and local no-go decisions cannot be traded for higher revenue or attendance.

reusable_rules.name: No universal green score
reusable_rules.rule: Keep energy, water, emissions, waste, habitat, local value and worker/community outcomes separate with units, boundaries, sources and uncertainty.

reusable_rules.name: Graceful closure is designed
reusable_rules.rule: Each venue needs explicit closure and recovery states, non-harmful alternatives, visitor communication and accountable human decision authority.

reusable_rules.name: No cultural copy-paste
reusable_rules.rule: Living culture, Indigenous knowledge, language, traditional access and cultural IP are locally governed; generic regional stereotypes are prohibited.

reusable_rules.name: Preserve future options
reusable_rules.rule: Compare phased, reversible, repurposable and exit pathways; evaluate irreversible commitments against multiple plausible futures and distributional downside. Do not optimize only for one forecast.

profiles.name: Tropical island and coral-coast destination
design_hypotheses: shaded outdoor routes with indoor storm alternatives
locally led maritime, food and craft experiences
reef interpretation without guaranteed wildlife encounters
hard_constraints: site-specific coastal hazard and evacuation approval
reef and nesting-species rules where applicable
customary beach access and local rights
closure_and_degraded_modes: storm shutdown with sheltered cultural/food/indoor program
non_assumptions: mangroves or reefs do not provide a universal substitute for engineered coastal protection
tourism revenue does not automatically accrue locally
tropical climate does not mean year-round safe sea conditions

profiles.name: Mediterranean and hot-summer coastal destination
design_hypotheses: water-sensitive gardens and reuse where safe and lawful
coastal retreat alternatives during extreme heat or fire risk
non_assumptions: beautiful weather is not a dependable year-round operating assumption
water recirculation does not erase freshwater consumption
heritage streets are not automatically suitable for higher visitor throughput

profiles.name: Temperate oceanic and mixed-weather beach destination
design_hypotheses: wind and rain tolerant promenade experiences
indoor surf, art or maker alternatives where justified
dune or wetland protection where ecologically appropriate
non_assumptions: coastal engineering solution transfers between beaches without analysis
a single seasonal peak can be supported without local transport capacity

profiles.name: Arid, semi-arid and water-stressed destination
design_hypotheses: night and dawn programming during hot periods
architecture based on shade, thermal mass and passive comfort where climate analysis supports it
dry adventure and immersive cooling effects rather than default large water bodies
key_drivers_to_measure: dust, wind and flash flood exposure
unknowns: water source lifecycle and marginal impacts
non_assumptions: desalination or reclaimed water is impact-free
large aquatic attractions are feasible because they can recirculate water
night events eliminate all heat, energy or neighbour impacts

profiles.name: Monsoon, wet-season and tropical-rain destination
key_drivers_to_measure: vector and public-health risk where relevant
non_assumptions: rainforest vegetation automatically stabilizes every slope
drainage alone makes development flood-safe
wet season can be treated as simply bad weather

profiles.name: Alpine ski and mountain resort
key_drivers_to_measure: natural snow reliability and snowpack duration
avalanche, landslide, wildfire and heat exposure
hard_constraints: ski lift and slope safety requirements
local hazard and weather closure rules
unknowns: seasonal viability under local climate projections
non_assumptions: snowmaking guarantees long-term ski viability
summer activities can fully replace winter revenue
climate resilience means only increasing snow production

profiles.name: Mountain destination designed for multiple seasons
design_hypotheses: distributed activity mix rather than one anchor season
non_assumptions: every mountain region should become a mass cycling destination
more visitors necessarily improve year-round local prosperity

profiles.name: Cruise ship, port, itinerary and host-community system
design_hypotheses: itinerary and arrival scheduling coordinated with destination capacity
lower-emission operations evaluated by full lifecycle boundary
local-led shore experiences with transparent value flow
accessible excursion variety and bad-weather alternatives
onboard and ashore crowd load treated together
key_drivers_to_measure: ship hotel/propulsion energy and fuel pathway
actual shore-power availability and grid mix
berth, terminal and shore transport capacity
wastewater, solid waste and air pollution handling
underwater noise and sensitive marine areas
visitor arrival pulses and heritage-site capacity
local spending retained and resident impact
closure_and_degraded_modes: overcapacity itinerary modification by accountable operator
unknowns: future fuel regulatory status and availability
non_assumptions: shore-power-ready ship means every port can supply it
a port call's spending all remains local
one vessel efficiency metric proves whole-voyage sustainability
a regulatory draft or approval is the same as entry into force
profiles.current_regulatory_note: IMO MEPC 84 in May 2026 recorded continued work after October 2025 adoption discussions were adjourned; verify live legal status before regulatory or investment decisions. EU FuelEU Maritime has specific scope and timing for qualifying passenger ships and covered ports.

profiles.name: Lake, river and wetland destination
design_hypotheses: shoreline recreation zones separate from sensitive habitat
water literacy and locally guided activities
key_drivers_to_measure: water quality and harmful bloom risk
non_assumptions: freshwater availability is abundant because a lake is visible
a natural water body is safe for recreation without monitoring

profiles.name: Temperate urban and peri-urban destination
design_hypotheses: reuse of existing buildings/land where life-cycle assessment supports it
key_drivers_to_measure: public transport and active travel capacity
non_assumptions: reusing a building is always lower-impact without assessment
more events are always compatible with urban life

profiles.name: Boreal, subarctic and northern destination
design_hypotheses: thermal comfort and rescue capability as core design
dark-sky and seasonal natural phenomena with honest viewing uncertainty
non_assumptions: aurora or wildlife sightings can be guaranteed
remote destinations can externalize waste and rescue costs

profiles.name: Savanna and semi-arid nature/cultural destination
design_hypotheses: community-governed guiding and conservation value sharing
hard_constraints: qualified wildlife viewing and emergency procedures
non_assumptions: wildlife is a guaranteed attraction
private conservation branding demonstrates ecological success
one safari model fits different communities or ecosystems

comparative_protocol.paired_comparison_rule: Same initial state, guest-demand assumptions, accounting boundaries and declared model versions; vary only the named intervention.
comparative_protocol.promotion_rule: Profiles remain hypotheses until site observations, local review, jurisdictional review, independent tests and fit-for-purpose field validation are complete.
